To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the secretory leukocyte inhibitor (SLPI), a serine protease inhibitor, has the potential to be developed as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of acute inflammatory diseases.
the suppressive effect of SLPI on intrapulmonary inflammation and neutrophil accumulation is related to its ability to suppress NF-kappaB activity.

mutant forms of the secretory leukocyte proteinase inhibitor (SLP) that have different degrees of protease inhibitory activity have different abilities to suppress the lung inflammatory response to IgG immune complexes.

the role of proteases in the pathophysiology of lung injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mutant forms of SLPI with different degrees of protease inhibitory activity have different abilities to suppress the lung inflammatory response.
the SLPI mutant with Lys(72)(replacing Leu72) was the most potent inhibitor of the lung vascular permeability and neutrophil accumulation.
the SLPI mutants that retained the capacity to bind and inactivate trypsin were effective inhibitors of the NF-kappaB-dependent neutrophil recruitment and vascular leak into the lungs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SLPI mutant with Leu(72), which had the most suppressiveness of the vascular leak and the recruitment of neutrophil into the lung, was the least effective in inhibiting trypsin, and the SLPI mutant which had the most inhibitory activity for trypsin, was the most suppressive of the lung vascular permeability and neutrophil accumulation.
the SLPI mutants with a higher trypsin-inhibition capacity were more potent in suppressing the lung vascular leak, neutrophils recruitment, and NF- kappaB activation than the WT SLPI.

the anti-inflammatory effects of SLPI are not limited to its protease inhibition activity but also extend to other activities, such as its ability to bind to the cell surface and to inhibit NF-kappaB.
